# core/csum.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/csum.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

Checksums over byte strings.

The Internet checksum (RFC 1071) that IPv4, ICMP, UDP and TCP headers
carry, and CRC-32 (the IEEE 802.3 polynomial, as Ethernet, zlib, PNG and
GPT use it). Both read a range `off..off+n` of a `Bytes`, so a packet
buffer is summed in place.

What is proved: every index is in bounds and every sum stays a 16-bit
(or 32-bit) value; one step of the ones'-complement sum is the sum
modulo 65535 (`csum_add`). Not proved: that the result is the checksum
the RFC defines over the whole range (the tests check known values).

`import "core/csum.bastio";`

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`csum_add`](#csum_add) | Adds the 16-bit word `v` to a ones'-complement sum `s` (end-around carry. |
| [`csum_sum16`](#csum_sum16) | The ones'-complement sum of bytes `off..off+n` of `b` as big-endian 16-bit words, added to `s0`. |
| [`csum_inet`](#csum_inet) | The Internet checksum of bytes `off..off+n`. |
| [`csum_pseudo4`](#csum_pseudo4) | The sum of an IPv4 pseudo-header (source and destination addresses, protocol, length), to start the sum of a UDP datagram or TCP segment. |
| [`crc32_update`](#crc32_update) | Continues a CRC-32 over bytes `off..off+n`. |
| [`crc32_start`](#crc32_start) | The running value a CRC-32 starts from. |
| [`crc32_end`](#crc32_end) | The finished CRC-32 of a running value. |
| [`crc32`](#crc32) | The CRC-32 of bytes `off..off+n` of `b`. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `csum_add`

```bastio
fn csum_add(s: u64, v: u64) -> u64
  requires s <= 65535 && v <= 65535
  ensures result <= 65535
  ensures (s + v <= 65535 ==> result == s + v) && (65535 < s + v ==> result == s + v - 65535)
```

Adds the 16-bit word `v` to a ones'-complement sum `s` (end-around
carry: a carry out of bit 15 is added back in at bit 0).

Example:

```bastio
let a = csum_add(4096, 1);
let b = csum_add(65535, 1);   // the carry wraps around
assert a == 4097 && b == 1;
```

### `csum_sum16`

```bastio
fn csum_sum16(b: &Bytes, off: u64, n: u64, s0: u64) -> u64
  requires off + n <= blen(b) && s0 <= 65535
  ensures result <= 65535
```

The ones'-complement sum of bytes `off..off+n` of `b` as big-endian
16-bit words, added to `s0`. An odd last byte is padded with a zero.

Example:

```bastio
// A 6-byte "header": two words of data and a checksum field, at first 0.
let mut h = balloc(6);
bset(&mut h, 0, 69);   // 0x45
bset(&mut h, 2, 18);   // 0x12
bset(&mut h, 3, 52);   // 0x34
let s = csum_sum16(h, 0, 6, 0);   // 0x4500 + 0x1234
let c = csum_inet(h, 0, 6);       // its complement
bset(&mut h, 4, cast[u8](c / 256));
bset(&mut h, 5, cast[u8](c % 256));
let z = csum_inet(h, 0, 6);       // a header holding its own checksum sums to 0
bfree(h);
if s != 22324 || c != 43211 || z != 0 { return 1; }
```

### `csum_inet`

```bastio
fn csum_inet(b: &Bytes, off: u64, n: u64) -> u64
  requires off + n <= blen(b)
  ensures result <= 65535
```

The Internet checksum of bytes `off..off+n`: the complement of their
sum. Over a header that already holds its own checksum it is 0.

### `csum_pseudo4`

```bastio
fn csum_pseudo4(src: u64, dst: u64, proto: u64, size: u64) -> u64
  requires src <= 4294967295 && dst <= 4294967295 && proto <= 255 && size <= 65535
  ensures result <= 65535
```

The sum of an IPv4 pseudo-header (source and destination addresses,
protocol, length), to start the sum of a UDP datagram or TCP segment:
`csum_sum16(b, off, size, csum_pseudo4(src, dst, proto, size))` is
65535 when the segment's checksum is right.

Example:

```bastio
// 10.0.0.1 to 10.0.0.2, UDP (17), 8 bytes.
let p = csum_pseudo4(167772161, 167772162, 17, 8);
if p != 5148 { return 1; }   // 0x0a00 + 0x0001 + 0x0a00 + 0x0002 + 17 + 8
```

### `crc32_update`

```bastio
fn crc32_update(c: u32, b: &Bytes, off: u64, n: u64) -> u32
  requires off + n <= blen(b)
```

Continues a CRC-32 over bytes `off..off+n`: `c` is the running value
(start with `crc32_start()`), the result goes into the next call or
into `crc32_end`. Bit by bit, with no table, so it needs no memory.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("123456789");
let whole = crc32(b, 0, 9);
// The same in two pieces, as for data that arrives in parts.
let mut c = crc32_start();
c = crc32_update(c, b, 0, 4);
c = crc32_update(c, b, 4, 5);
let parts = crc32_end(c);
bfree(b);
if whole != 3421780262 || parts != whole { return 1; }   // 0xcbf43926, the standard check value
```

### `crc32_start`

```bastio
fn crc32_start() -> u32
```

The running value a CRC-32 starts from.

### `crc32_end`

```bastio
fn crc32_end(c: u32) -> u32
```

The finished CRC-32 of a running value.

### `crc32`

```bastio
fn crc32(b: &Bytes, off: u64, n: u64) -> u32
  requires off + n <= blen(b)
```

The CRC-32 of bytes `off..off+n` of `b`.
